<h2 id="tocS_Status">Status</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastatus"></a>
<a id="schema_Status"></a>
<a id="tocSstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsstatus"></a>

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "details": [
    {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }
  ],
  "message": "string"
}
```

The `Status` type defines a logical error model that is suitable for different programming environments, including REST APIs and RPC APIs. It is used by [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc). Each `Status` message contains three pieces of data: error code, error message, and error details. You can find out more about this error model and how to work with it in the [API Design Guide](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|integer(int32)|false|none|The status code, which should be an enum value of google.rpc.Code.|
|details|[object]|false|none|A list of messages that carry the error details. There is a common set of message types for APIs to use.|
|message|string|false|none|A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the google.rpc.Status.details field, or localized by the client.|

<h2 id="tocS_TargetingExpansionConfig">TargetingExpansionConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematargetingexpansionconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_TargetingExpansionConfig"></a>
<a id="tocStargetingexpansionconfig"></a>
<a id="tocstargetingexpansionconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "excludeFirstPartyAudience": true,
  "targetingExpansionLevel": "TARGETING_EXPANSION_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED"
}
```

Settings that control the targeting expansion of the line item. Targeting expansion allows the line item to reach a larger audience based on the original audience list and the targeting expansion level. Beginning **March 25, 2023**, these settings may represent the [optimized targeting feature](//support.google.com/displayvideo/answer/12060859) in place of targeting expansion. This feature will be rolled out to all partners by early May 2023.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|excludeFirstPartyAudience|boolean|false|none|Required. Whether to exclude first-party audiences from use in targeting expansion or optimized targeting. Similar audiences of the excluded first-party lists will not be excluded. Only applicable when a first-party audience is positively targeted (directly or included in a combined audience), otherwise this selection will be ignored. Beginning **March 25, 2023**, this field may be deprecated with the replacement of targeting expansion with [optimized targeting](//support.google.com/displayvideo/answer/12060859). Upon deprecation, this field will be set to `false`. If this field is set to `true` when deprecated, all positive first-party audience targeting assigned to this line item will be replaced with negative targeting of the same first-party audiences to ensure the continued exclusion of those audiences. This field will be deprecated for all partners by early May 2023.|
|targetingExpansionLevel|string|false|none|Required. Magnitude of expansion for applicable targeting under this line item. Beginning **March 25, 2023**, the behavior of this field may change in the following ways with the replacement of targeting expansion with [optimized targeting](//support.google.com/displayvideo/answer/12060859): * This field will represent the optimized targeting checkbox, with a `NO_EXPANSION` value representing optimized targeting turned off and a `LEAST_EXPANSION` value representing optimized targeting turned on. * `NO_EXPANSION` will be the default value for the field and will be automatically assigned if you do not set the field. * If you set the field to any value other than `NO_EXPANSION`, it will automatically be set to `LEAST_EXPANSION`. This behavior will be rolled out to all partners by early May 2023.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|targetingExpansionLevel|TARGETING_EXPANSION_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED|

Settings that control the bid strategy for YouTube and Partners resources.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|adGroupEffectiveTargetCpaSource|string|false|read-only|Output only. Source of the effective targetCpa value for AdGroup.|
|adGroupEffectiveTargetCpaValue|string(int64)|false|read-only|Output only. The effective targetCpa for AdGroup, in micros of advertiser's currency.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the bidding strategy.|
|value|string(int64)|false|none|The value used by the bidding strategy. When the bidding strategy is assigned at the line item level, this field is only applicable for the following strategy types: * `YOUTUBE_AND_PARTNERS_BIDDING_STRATEGY_TYPE_TARGET_CPA` When the bidding strategy is assigned at the ad group level, this field is only applicable for the following strategy types: * `YOUTUBE_AND_PARTNERS_BIDDING_STRATEGY_TYPE_MANUAL_CPM` * `YOUTUBE_AND_PARTNERS_BIDDING_STRATEGY_TYPE_MANUAL_CPV` * `YOUTUBE_AND_PARTNERS_BIDDING_STRATEGY_TYPE_TARGET_CPA` * `YOUTUBE_AND_PARTNERS_BIDDING_STRATEGY_TYPE_TARGET_CPM` If not using an applicable strategy, the value of this field will be 0.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|adGroupEffectiveTargetCpaSource|BIDDING_SOURCE_LINE_ITEM|

|type|YOUTUBE_AND_PARTNERS_BIDDING_STRATEGY_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|type|YOUTUBE_AND_PARTNERS_BIDDING_STRATEGY_TYPE_MANUAL_CPV|
|type|YOUTUBE_AND_PARTNERS_BIDDING_STRATEGY_TYPE_MANUAL_CPM|
|type|YOUTUBE_AND_PARTNERS_BIDDING_STRATEGY_TYPE_TARGET_CPA|
|type|YOUTUBE_AND_PARTNERS_BIDDING_STRATEGY_TYPE_TARGET_CPM|
|type|YOUTUBE_AND_PARTNERS_BIDDING_STRATEGY_TYPE_MAXIMIZE_LIFT|
|type|YOUTUBE_AND_PARTNERS_BIDDING_STRATEGY_TYPE_MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS|
